briefing.opening: Hello everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 3, 2026.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Change Adaptation and Agricultural Crisis Response
sections.content: Domestically, proactive response efforts are active [2] as concerns grow over agricultural disasters and worsening food security due to climate change. In particular, Gangwon Province announced plans to invest 147 billion KRW to respond to agricultural disasters and firmly support agricultural disaster policy insurance [1, 4, 5]. These efforts are essential for mitigating direct damages caused by climate change and enhancing the resilience of local communities. Furthermore, Minister Kim Seong-hwan met with the CEO of the Children's Investment Fund Foundation (CIFF), a global philanthropic foundation supporting climate change and child welfare, to explore international cooperation strategies [3].

sections.title: 🔴 International Climate Litigation and Increasing Direct Impacts
sections.content: Internationally, legal disputes over liability for damages caused by climate change are intensifying. The U.S. Supreme Court is set to hear a major climate change lawsuit related to devastating wildfires in Colorado [19, 22, 26, 28, 31, 32, 34, 35], which could set an important precedent for assigning legal responsibility for the climate crisis [20, 24, 27, 29, 30]. The International Court of Justice is also addressing climate change-related issues [21], drawing attention to the international community's movement towards achieving climate justice. Meanwhile, it was announced at EADV 2026 that climate change is linked to global changes in skin diseases [25], the worst-ever bluetongue outbreak has hit farms in the UK [37], and direct impacts are spreading, such as streets in Bangkok, Thailand, turning into stagnant lakes due to floods [38].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Renewable Energy Transition and Accelerating Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Domestically, diverse efforts are underway to transition to renewable energy to achieve carbon neutrality goals. The Korea Energy Agency is exploring ways to verify the performance of climate policies for greenhouse gas reduction, thereby enhancing policy effectiveness [6]. In the Goheung and Yeosu regions, a 'citizen grand compromise' has begun to usher in a 10GW era of renewable energy [10, 16], and Jeju Energy Corporation has embarked on developing clean hydrogen production technology to respond to renewable energy variability, securing new momentum for energy transition [11, 14]. Incheon citizens are actively participating, presenting a blueprint for a 'Carbon-Neutral Smart Ocean City' by 2045 [9], demonstrating vibrant citizen-led carbon neutrality initiatives [7]. Amidst these trends, global capital is focusing on renewable energy consulting and technology sectors [12], and the multi-outlet power strip market is also projected to grow at an average annual rate of 6-9% until 2035, driven by demand from data centers and renewable energy [15], indicating an acceleration in the growth of the renewable energy industry [13, 17, 18].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges Threatening Carbon Neutrality Goals and International Response
sections.content: Efforts by the international community and domestic entities to achieve carbon neutrality goals are simultaneously facing new challenges. Domestically, the potential conflict between the goal of becoming an 'AI powerhouse' and 'carbon neutrality' has emerged as a debate surrounding the energy consumption of AI data centers [8]. The European Union (EU) is strengthening its climate adaptation efforts [23], and the consideration of climate change is becoming increasingly important in major policy decisions, such as environmental concerns raised regarding the expansion of Heathrow Airport in the UK [39]. Meanwhile, a Fijian climate activist delivered a message urging 'action' ahead of a UN meeting in the Pacific [40], representing the voices of vulnerable nations. On a positive note, Bangladesh achieved historic success at the International Climate Change Olympiad held in Russia in 2026 [36], highlighting the importance of climate change education and awareness.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlights the need to acknowledge the severe impacts of climate change, accelerate adaptation and mitigation efforts, and wisely respond to new challenges. This concludes today's climate briefing.

articles.original_title: Worst ever outbreak of bluetongue hits British farms
articles.description: Climate crisis blamed as virus that originated in Africa spreads to livestock as far north as AberdeenshireBritish farmers are experiencing the worst bluetongue season on record, with the number of cases surpassing the past three years combined.The viral disease, which affects sheep and cattle among other animals, can cause fevers, ulcers, a swollen head and lameness. The tongue may go blue and even protrude from the mouth. In the most severe cases, the animal can die. Continue reading...

articles.title: The expansion of Heathrow would be an expensive disaster for Britain and the world. Burnham needs to block it | George Monbiot
articles.description: A third runway would fly in the face of reason. If we are to prioritise human life over short-term ‘growth’, we need to use planes less, not more If a third runway is built at Heathrow, what will be the impact on the wealth of the nation? It will cost us somewhere between £23.4bn and £62.5bn. These are not my figures; they weren’t calculated by environmental groups, but by the Department for Transport.For decades, government ministers have told us that airport expansion is essential for “growth”

articles.title: ‘We want action’: Fijian climate activist sends message ahead of UN talks in Pacific
articles.description: Lavenia Naivalu has seen the impact of the climate crisis first-hand and is determined to amplify Pacific voices at this year’s pre-Cop summit in FijiFrom her wooden veranda in Fiji’s remote Yasawa islands, climate activist Lavenia Naivalu remembers when the reefs were once so healthy, her grandfather would walk to the shoreline and return with fish. But life there has changed.“The reefs that the older generation of men spearfished in, no longer provide what they once did,” the 44-year-old says.
